title: The Assassination Of A Reformed Government Official Zien Ying-Ching

page_data.en:
Hwa Mei Wan Pao of December 1 :-

THE ASSASSINATION OF A "REFORMED GOVERNMENT" OFFICIAL

Zien Ying-ching (錢應清) alias Zien Ching-ping (錢鏡平), Chief of the Debenture Department of the Ministry of Finance of the "Reformed Government", was attacked at his residence at No.10, Lane 46, Zau Ka Kiao (趙家橋), Hart Road, at 9 a.m. November 29, and died in the Red Cross Hospital on Avenue Haig. He was a native of Tsungming, aged 63. He obtained the degree of B.A. in the Tsing Dynasty and studied in Waseda University of Japan at the expense of the government. His eldest son is the engineer who constructed the Chientang Bridge.

During the regime of the Pei Yang warlords, Zien Ying-ching was Chief of the Currency Bureau and he misappropriated more than a million dollars. A warrant for his arrest was issued by Yuan Shih-kai but this was withdrawn upon payment of $300,000. At one time he was in charge of the Ministry of Finance when Chen Lu (陳錄) was Vice Minister. Chen Lu is at present Minister of Finance of the "Reformed Government". It was he who appointed Zien Ying-ching as Chief of the Debenture Department. Zien was also a Director of the China South Sea Bank of which he was a large shareholder.

12月1日《华美晚报》：

“维新政府”官员遇刺案

“维新政府”财政部公债司司长钱应清（别名钱镜平）于11月29日上午9时，在哈同路赵家桥46弄10号寓所遭袭击，后在海格大道红十字会医院身亡。钱系崇明人，享年63岁。清代举人出身，曾由公费派往日本早稻田大学留学。其长子为建造钱塘江大桥的工程师。

在北洋军阀统治时期，钱应清曾任币制局总裁，侵吞公款逾百万元。袁世凯曾签发逮捕令，但在其缴纳30万元后撤销。钱应清一度主持财政部工作，当时陈录任副部长。陈录现任“维新政府”财政部长，正是由他任命钱应清为公债司司长。钱还担任中国南海银行董事，是该行的大股东。

November 30, 1938. Morning Translation

Standard and other local newspapers .-

ASSASSINATION OF A "REFORMED GOVERNMENT" OFFICIAL

Yesterday a murder took place in house No.10,
Lane 64, Zau Ka Kiao (趙家橋), Hart Road, the victim
being an official of the "Reformed Government".
Enquiries made by our reporter elicited the
following information.- Zien Ching-ping (錢鏡平), age 63,
native of Tsungming, lived with his wife, Zien Sung Sz
(錢沈氏), age 40, at House No.10, Lane 64, Zau Ka Kiao,
Hart Road. He had served as a Departmental Chief of the
Ministry of Finance in the 4th year of the Chinese Republic
(1915) when Yuan Shih-kai was President. After giving up
his political career, he devoted himself to philanthropic
enterprises and had served on the committees of the Sing
Vee Relief Society (辛未救濟會), the Yellow River Flood
Relief Association and the Federation of Charitable Bodies.
He was also an ardent promoter of Buddhism. He had been
living at the present address since the outbreak of the
Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai. Following the
occupation of Shanghai and the establishment of puppet
regimes, he was appointed Chief of the Debenture Department
of the Ministry of Finance of the "Reformed Government"
under the name of Zien Ying-ching (錢應清).
At 9 a.m. yesterday three men, one armed with
a pistol and the other two with axes, entered Zien's home
and attacked Zien who was still in bed. He was struck
in the head, hands, shoulders and chest and was rendered
unconscious. His wife was also hit twice. The three men
made good their escape. The injured couple were later
removed to the Red Cross Hospital on Avenue Haig where the
man succumbed at 3 p.m. while the wife was discharged after
having her injuries dressed. The Police are investigating
the affair.

《标准报》及其他本地报纸。-

“维新政府”官员遇刺案

昨日，在哈特路（Hart Road）赵家桥64弄10号发生了一起谋杀案，受害者系一名“维新政府”官员。经本报记者调查，获悉如下信息。- 钱镜平，63岁，崇明人，与其妻钱沈氏（40岁）同住于哈特路赵家桥64弄10号。民国四年（1915年）袁世凯任总统期间，他曾担任财政部司长。弃政后，他投身慈善事业，曾任职于辛未救济会、黄河水灾救济协会以及慈善团体联合会的委员会。他也是佛教的热心倡导者。自上海中日战事爆发以来，他一直居住于现址。上海沦陷及伪政权建立后，他以钱应清之名被任命为“维新政府”财政部公债司司长。
昨日上午9时，三名男子闯入钱宅，其中一人持手枪，另两人持斧头，袭击了尚在床上的钱某。其头部、手部、肩部及胸部遭击打，陷入昏迷。其妻亦被击打两次。三名男子随即逃脱。受伤夫妇随后被送往海格大道红十字会医院，男子于下午3时伤重不治身亡，妻子则在伤口包扎后出院。警方正在调查此案。

At 8.15 a.m. 29-11-38 Zung Hoen Tsang(陳華章),
residing at No 64/10 ... Koo Road (near Hart Road)
came to the station and reported that at 8.15 a.m.
three strangers entered his house to murder his
nephew and ... Tsiang Ming(錢鏡子) at the above
address.

... ambulance was summoned. At the same
time detectives went to the above address and
learned the following:-

No 64/10 ... Koo Road is occupied by Tien
Ching ... who was Assistant Commissioner in the
Ministry of Finance in Imperial Government at Peking
up to the formation of the Chinese Republic in 1911.
Since that time he has lived at various addresses in
Shanghai, and is said to have kept out of political
affairs. His second wife Tien Sung Sz(錢松氏).
twelve relatives of various degrees and three maid
servants share the house. Formerly Tien Ching Ming
was a wealthy man but during the last few years has
lost much money and is now living economically. He
has an aversion to meeting strangers and when any
call they are told that he is out and requested to
call again.

At about 8.15 a.m. 29-11-38 three strangers as
described on Sheet No.1, entered the house through
the open front door and met Tien Iung Tung(李应诚)
(complainant's nephew) and Zung Hoen Tsang(complt's
distant nephew) in the guestroom. One of the three

strangers, probably the 1st described, produced an
addressed letter which he said had come from Hongkew,
and asked for the "master" and then for "Mr. Zien".
Zien Lung Zung in accordance with instructions said that
Mr. Zien was not at home. Upon this, another of the
strangers, probably the 2nd described, produced a short
pistol and herded both Zien Lung Zung and Zung Hoen Tsang
into a small wing room at the back and closed the door
in them. Three amahs and the complainant's son, aged 9
years, were in the kitchen. The three men paid no
attention to them but searched the front wing room for
Mr. Zien Ching Bing.

The three strangers then went upstairs to the
complainant's bedroom on the first floor. Two of them
entered and dragged the old man from his bed to the land-
ing where one of them held the complainant's wrists while
the other hacked at his head with an axe. The complt's.
wife Zien Sung Sz, who was in another bed in the same
room, stated that the first stranger appeared to be unarm
ed but the second flourished an axe. She hurried after
them to the landing and in attempting to save her husband
she received axe injuries to her head and left hand.

While the murderers were hacking at the complainant'
head, the axe fell off the haft. They then left their
victim and made good their escape after being on the
premises about two minutes.

几名陌生人，可能是上述第一名嫌疑人，拿出一封有地址的信件，称该信来自虹口（Hongkew），并要求见“主人”，随后又要求见“Zien先生”。曾龙宗（Zien Lung Zung）按照指示称Zien先生不在家。随即，另一名陌生人，可能是上述第二名嫌疑人，掏出一支短手枪，将曾龙宗和曾洪藏（Zung Hoen Tsang）赶进后面的一间小厢房，并将门关上。当时厨房里有三名女佣和报案人九岁的儿子。这三名男子未加理会，而是在前厢房搜寻曾清炳（Zien Ching Bing）先生。

随后，这三名陌生人上楼来到位于二楼的报案人卧室。其中两人进入房间，将老人从床上拖至楼梯平台，一人按住报案人的手腕，另一人则用斧头砍击其头部。报案人之妻曾宋氏（Zien Sung Sz）当时在同屋的另一张床上，她陈述称，第一名陌生人似乎未携带武器，但第二名陌生人挥舞着一把斧头。她急忙追至楼梯平台，在试图营救丈夫时，头部和左手被斧头砍伤。

当凶手砍击报案人头部时，斧头从柄上脱落。随后他们丢下受害者，在屋内停留约两分钟后成功逃脱。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

The remainder of the household came to the assist-
ance of Zien Ching Ming or his wife. At the same time
Zien Jun Ming (nephew) telephoned to the complainant's
daughter Mrs. Zien (程錢氏) at 144 R. Reid, and asked
her to come to the house. After she had arrived it was
decided upon to call the police.

Both injured persons were taken to the Chinese Red
Cross Hospital, Avenue Foch, and certified as follows:

Zien Ching Ming: "Lacerated wound of scalp and
compound fracture of skull.
Condition critical."

Zien Song Zi: "Lacerated wound of right face and
left hand. Condition fair."

All relatives and servants living in the complt's.
house were questioned. Only one suggestion of a
possible motive was obtained. Sung Bing Wei (沈炳万)
(brother-in-law by complainant's 2nd wife) stated that
about three months ago while he was in Da Tsung Sung
(大椿鎮), Soongning (complainant's native place), he met
another distant nephew of the complainant's named Loh
Siao Zi (陸小仕), who mentioned in an off-hand way that
Zien Ching Ming (complainant) had been invited by some-
body unknown to join the Reformed Government at Nanking.
No further details were available as Loh Siao Zi is not
in Shanghai. Efforts to obtain details of visitors to
the complainant's home and his outside activities

produced nothing relevant. The complainant appears not
to have had any visitors outside the family and close-
friend circle. Daily he attends the "Pure Karma
Buddists" Association at 418 Hart Road, and is not known
to have other interests.

Enquiries were made in Zao Ka Jao Road in the
neighbourhood of Lane 64, but no witnesses of the
arrival and departure of the murderers were found.

Detectives will keep in contact with the complt's.
family, and the complainant will be carefully questioned
should he recover from his injuries.

The general impression gained is that the complt's.
household know more than they are prepared to tell at the
moment. It is unlikely that he could be approached
concerning participation in the Reformed Government with-
out others apart from Loh Siao Z knowing.

CHINA PRESS.
NOV 30 1938
Another Local
Gov't Official
Assassinated
Bond Office Executive
Dies After Attack
By Axe Killers
Zee Ching-ping, 61, head of the
bond and loan office maintained by
the finance department of the
"Shanghai City Government," and
formerly an official of the old
Peking Government, is dead while
his wife is in the Chinese Red Cross
Hospital receiving treatment for
severe axe wounds about the face
and body.
The wounds were inflicted by
three would-be assassins who enter-
ed the Zee home, House 10, Lane
64, Hart Road, about 9 a.m. yes-
terday. One of the assailants was
armed with a pistol while the other
two carried axes.
After forcing their way past the
servants of the Zee household, the
thugs entered the living room and
grabbed both the man and his wife.
They threw the aged couple to the
floor, sat on them and proceeded
to hack both victims about the face,
hands and arms.
Mrs. Zee sustained two severe
wounds to the head and a bad cut
on the right arm. Mr. Zee was cut
about the arms, side and cheeks.
While the attack against the
couple was underway, a servant
managed to raise an alarm where-
upon the three would-be killers took
to their heels. They had disappear-
ed completely before the police ar-
rived on the scene. Both of the
victims were rushed by emergency
ambulance to the Chinese Red
Cross Hospital.
Despite the efforts of attending
surgeons and physicians, Zee died
yesterday afternoon, several hours
after his arrival at the hospital.
His wife was still alive last night
but her condition is reported to be
serious.
Up to a late hour last night the
police had established no definite
motive for the killing. Because of
Zee's connections with the "Shang-
hai City Government," however, it
is believed that the attack bears
considerable political significance.

《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）。
1938年11月30日
又一名地方政府官员
遇刺身亡
公债办事处主管
遭斧头杀手袭击后死亡
谢景平（Zee Ching-ping），61岁，“上海市政府”财政局下属公债与贷款办事处主任，前北洋政府官员，在其妻子因面部和身体遭受严重斧伤在中国红十字会医院接受治疗期间死亡。

伤口系由三名企图行凶的刺客造成，他们于昨日上午9时许进入位于哈同路（Hart Road）64弄10号的谢宅。其中一名袭击者持有手枪，另外两人携带斧头。

在强行突破谢家仆人的阻拦后，暴徒闯入客厅，抓住了谢某及其妻子。他们将这对老夫妇推倒在地，坐在他们身上，随即开始砍击两名受害者的面部、手部和手臂。

谢太太头部受两处重伤，右臂有一处严重割伤。谢先生手臂、侧身和脸颊被砍伤。

在对夫妇二人实施袭击的过程中，一名仆人设法发出警报，随后三名企图行凶者逃之夭夭。在警察到达现场之前，他们已完全消失。两名受害者均由急救救护车紧急送往中国红十字会医院。

尽管主治外科医生和医师全力抢救，谢某仍于昨日下午，即抵达医院数小时后死亡。其妻子昨晚尚在人世，但据报道情况危急。

截至昨晚深夜，警方尚未确定谋杀的确切动机。然而，鉴于谢某与“上海市政府”的关系，人们认为此次袭击具有相当重要的政治意义。
